article_title: Partnerships that Work: Tapping Research to Address Learner Variability in Young Readers
citation: Tare, M., Nobles, S., & Xiao, W. (2018). Partnerships that work: Tapping research to address learner variability in young readers. Washington, DC: Digital Promise Global. https://www.digitalpromise.org/
title: LPS-edtech developer partnership process for research-based product improvement
description: LPS partnerships with developers follow a collaborative process: explore the mission and goals of the existing product; review product features against LPS to identify supports for learner variability; create an assessment report highlighting key potential improvements; co-create a development plan and timeline; implement product features; conduct research to assess how new features support more learner variability; and cross-promote to advance research-based products. Features are categorized into short-, mid-, and long-term phases of development aligned with the partner's roadmap.
requirements: Partner organizations committed to reaching learners from a variety of backgrounds and with varying needs
constraints: The first set of partnerships specifically sought products focused on readers in pre-kindergarten through third grade to leverage the Reading PK-3 model
target_learners: Pre-K through third grade readers with varying needs
target_learning_goals: Reading achievement supported by evidence-based product features
examples: The ReadWorks partnership produced a draft assessment report finalized jointly, with features phased into the product roadmap
key_sources: Tare, M., Nobles, S., & Xiao, W. (2018). Partnerships that work: Tapping research to address learner variability in young readers. Washington, DC: Digital Promise Global. https://digitalpromise.dspacedirect.org/items/e59c6e47-4209-4187-a0ef-b8da08283ec6

article_title: To Grade or Not To Grade? Demystifying a Centuries-Old Debate
citation: Nicolas Hübner, Juliane Rutsch, Ann-Kathrin Schnelle, Mia Herkommer, Evelin Ruth-Herbein, Benjamin Fauth. (2026). To Grade or Not To Grade? Demystifying a Centuries-Old Debate. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10156-1
title: LPF school trial: grade abolishment with standards-based competency grids, learning-development meetings, and formative feedback
description: The Learning-enhanced Performance Feedback (LPF) school trial was a quasi-experimental intervention in 35 Baden-Württemberg elementary schools beginning in the 2022/2023 school year, compared with 40 control schools. Trial schools abolished written grades and report cards and instead gave "standards-based competency grids" on a 4-point scale from "You still need to work on this" to "You are an expert", at least two oral learning-development meetings per school year, and formative assessment and feedback practices integrated throughout instruction. The grids share many similarities with standards-based grading systems as defined by Welsh et al. (2013) and Guskey and Bailey (2001).
requirements: Trial schools were required to eliminate written grades from Grade 2 onward; implementation was evaluated on behalf of the Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs
constraints: The trial was implemented with minimal requirements: teachers received no comprehensive professional development and no detailed guidance on formative assessment or feedback practices; standardization of features decreased from the first to the third feature
examples: Competency grids covered predefined areas in German, mathematics, and social studies (e.g., "You read texts fluently", "You can measure sizes") plus behavior, work attitude, and learning process
key_sources: Nicolas Hübner, Juliane Rutsch, Ann-Kathrin Schnelle, Mia Herkommer, Evelin Ruth-Herbein, Benjamin Fauth. (2026). To Grade or Not To Grade? Demystifying a Centuries-Old Debate. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10156-1

article_title: Feuerstein's Mediated Learning Experience as a Vehicle for Enhancing Cognitive Functioning of Remedial School Learners in South Africa
citation: Seabi, J. (2012). Feuerstein's mediated learning experience as a vehicle for enhancing cognitive functioning of remedial school learners in South Africa. Australian Journal of Educational & Developmental Psychology, 12, 35-45. http://www.newcastle.edu.au/journal/ajedp/
title: LPAD Set Variations B-8 to B-12 mediation tasks with the Raven's Coloured Progressive Matrices
description: The study used two instruments from the Learning Potential Assessment Device. The LPAD Set Variations B-8 to B-12 consist of sets of six variations on five Raven's Coloured Progressive Matrices items and were selected because "they permit the examiner to access and to modify the area of abstract thinking, and also represent tasks that under normal circumstances are rarely offered to the low-functioning individual." The RCPM, a nonverbal problem-solving test with sets A, AB and B scored 0 to 36, served as the pre- and post-measure (sets A and AB, scores 0 to 24), with set B used for mediation. Both measure forming comparisons, reasoning by analogy and organising spatial perceptions.
requirements: Standard administration of the RCPM in group setting for pre- and post-test phases
Examiner training in LPAD mediation procedures
constraints: The RCPM has been standardized only in the United Kingdom, the United States of America and Germany, though South African studies support it as a measure of intellectual functioning
target_learners: Low-functioning learners and learners with learning difficulties
target_learning_goals: Abstract thinking, analogical reasoning, comparison-forming and spatial organisation
examples: Problems A and AB of the RCPM were used as pre-post measurements while set B served as the mediation task
key_sources: Seabi, J. (2012). Feuerstein's mediated learning experience as a vehicle for enhancing cognitive functioning of remedial school learners in South Africa. Australian Journal of Educational & Developmental Psychology, 12, 35-45. http://www.newcastle.edu.au/journal/ajedp/
